en.title: God of War Laufey Star Unbothered by Backlash: 'I know it's great'
en.summary: Despite some negative online reactions to the upcoming God of War title focusing on Laufey, star Deborah Ann Woll remains unfazed. She expressed confidence in the game's quality, stating she feels 'totally unbothered' by the criticism.
en.body:
The announcement of a new direction for the **God of War** franchise, shifting focus to **Laufey**, has ignited a predictable wave of online discourse. While many fans are eager to explore new narratives within the beloved series, a vocal minority has expressed disappointment with the departure from **Kratos**'s central role. Amidst this, **Deborah Ann Woll**, reprising her role as **Laufey** after her impactful performance in **God of War Ragnarök**, has addressed the backlash directly, revealing a remarkable lack of concern.

At a recent appearance at Florida Supercon, **Woll** was questioned about the negative reactions to the game's reveal. Her response, captured by TikTok influencer quinnphobic, showcased a calm and assured perspective. She admitted that while she anticipated being more affected, her distance from social media and a strong conviction in the game's quality have left her "totally unbothered." "It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad," **Woll** stated, underscoring her belief in the project's merit regardless of dissenting opinions.

## A New Era for the Norse Saga

The shift towards **Laufey** as the protagonist marks a significant evolution for the **God of War** series. While **Kratos** has been the stoic, vengeful heart of the franchise since its inception on the PlayStation 2, the recent Norse saga introduced a more paternal and introspective side to the character. The reveal trailer for the **Laufey**-centric game showcased a departure in combat style and narrative focus, hinting at a deeper exploration of the character's origins and motivations. This move, while potentially alienating some who crave more of the "mad lad turned sad dad" persona, aligns with the series' established trajectory of character development and thematic exploration. The prospect of navigating the afterlife with a unique companion, as suggested by the trailer, offers a fresh take that could revitalize the franchise.

## Fan Reactions and Franchise Evolution

The online reaction to the **God of War Laufey** announcement has been a microcosm of broader trends in gaming communities. While the core appeal of the series has always been its brutal combat and epic storytelling, the fanbase is diverse, encompassing both those deeply invested in the lore and those drawn to the visceral gameplay. The criticism directed at the new direction often stems from a desire to see **Kratos**'s story continue in a familiar vein. However, **Sony Santa Monica** has consistently demonstrated a commitment to pushing narrative boundaries, as seen in the acclaimed reboots of the franchise. The studio has also assured fans that **Kratos** will indeed return in future installments, suggesting that this new focus on **Laufey** is an expansion rather than an abandonment of the established characters and world.

## What's Next

While specific details regarding the full scope of **Laufey**'s story and the overarching narrative for the next **God of War** installment are still emerging, the game is slated for a 2026 release. Fans can anticipate further updates from **Sony Santa Monica** as development progresses, offering more insight into this exciting new chapter for the acclaimed franchise.

content_raw: In a depressingly predictable turn of events, the reveal God of War Laufey came under fire from certain corners of the Internet, as it centres around a female protagonist rather than mad lad turned sad dad Kratos. Much of this negative reaction has centred around Laufey's actor Deborah Ann Woll, who also played Laufey in the 2018 reboot. But Woll, who also plays Karen Page in Marvel's Daredevil and its reboot Daredevil: Born Again, isn't phased by the impotent rage of misogynistic online trolls: Woll was asked about the backlash to the game's reveal by TikTok influencer quinnphobic at Florida Supercon (via Eurogamer ) who recorded the actor's response for TikTok : "Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more affected by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll replied. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad." I'll admit to being surprised by Sony Santa Monica's direction for the next God of War , since Kratos has been at the centre of it since the very beginning. But having watched the lengthy reveal trailer/game demo, you can hardly say it isn't in the spirit of the franchise. The idea of carving my way through the afterlife with a big wobbly cube companion seems rad, and if anything, Laufey is truer to the series' original design philosophy than the more recent reboots, returning to a more traditional combat system I felt like the Norse setting had run its course by the end of God of War: Ragnarök , and some new blood was needed for the series to continue. Besides, Sony Santa Monica has said that Kratos will return in future games anyway . So why be mad? Of course, we know why some people are mad, and it has nothing to do with the quality of the game. What I will be mad at, however, is if God of War Laufey doesn't come to PC. Both God of War and Ragnarök saw a delayed PC release after Sony discovered that launching its PlayStation exclusives on Steam et al is like printing money . But in May, Sony said it is retreating from the PC as a platform as it recommits to PlayStation exclusives being, well, exclusive. This would suggest that Laufey will be stuck on PS5 (or possibly PS6 by the time it launches). Personally, though, I don't see this decision lasting all that long.
